title: SDKS mini-atelier: ergonomic streaming & retry starter examples for Next.js / FastAPI / Go / CLI
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal:
Ship a compact, opinionated set of starter examples (Next.js app, FastAPI microservice, Go HTTP server, and a cross-platform CLI) that demonstrate ergonomic streaming, deterministic retries with idempotency, and recommended patterns for production usage of Redwood SDKs. The artifacts should be lightweight, runnable locally, and serve as canonical snippets for docs and onboarding.

Scope and trade-offs:
- Focus on end-to-end developer ergonomics over covering every API surface. Provide 4 curated examples rather than exhaustive language bindings.
- Include: streaming generation with backpressure-friendly consumers, resumable retries for intermittent network errors, idempotency key patterns for non-idempotent calls (billing/side-effects), and simple unit/integration tests.
- Do not implement server-side infra for private deployments; keep samples agnostic to deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private).

Acceptance criteria (must pass before marking Done):
1) Repo contains four directories: nextjs/, fastapi/, go-server/, cli/ with README and run instructions.
2) Each example demonstrates: streaming response consumption, client-side automatic retry with exponential backoff and jitter, and safe manual retry using idempotency keys.
3) Automated smoke test (CI) runs examples in a lightweight mode (mocked endpoint or Redwood sandbox) and verifies streaming tokens flow, retry logic triggers on injected errors, and idempotency avoids duplicate side-effects.
4) Docs PR created that links to each example and copies the concise snippets for quickstart pages.
5) API ergonomics validated by 2 external engineers (feedback cycle recorded in comments).
6) Example CLIs support both sync and streaming modes and include a simple local cache for short-term prefix caching demo.

Implementation notes and decisions:
- Streaming: use unified ergonomic helpers in each language that expose an async iterator (Python/TS) or channel (Go) and include a convenience line-by-line helper for terminal demos.
- Retries: implement an opinionated RetryPolicy with configurable max_retries, base_delay, max_delay, and jitter. Include demonstration of when to disable retries for certain status codes (4xx vs 5xx) and how to bubble up non-retryable errors.
- Idempotency: show generator request with an explicit idempotency_key header and a side-effect simulation (e.g., local file append inside FastAPI) to show safe reruns.
- Testing: CI to use a small mock server that injects transient failures to exercise retry/backoff; use real streaming semantics where possible (chunked responses).
- SDK dependencies: pin to latest sdk-2026.03 minor, and include a short migration note for older SDK versions.

Deliverables:
- examples/nextjs: minimal Next.js page that streams tokens into a React component with graceful reconnect and resume example.
- examples/fastapi: async FastAPI endpoint that proxies Redwood streaming responses and demonstrates idempotent webhook-like flow.
- examples/go-server: simple net/http server that consumes streaming responses and forwards events to SSE endpoint.
- examples/cli: small cross-platform CLI (Go or Node) that can run in interactive streaming mode or one-shot with retries and local caching.
- docs/snippets.md: one-page markdown with copy-paste snippets for streaming, retries, and idempotency per language.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: scaffold examples, core helpers (RetryPolicy, StreamReader), and README drafts.
- Week 2: implement tests, CI mock harness, and iterate on ergonomics from feedback.
- Week 3: finalize docs and create public samples repo PR.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: streaming semantics differ across runtimes -> mitigation: provide small adapter layer that normalizes the pattern.
- Risk: too many knobs confuse users -> mitigation: opinionated defaults and a short section in each README explaining the recommended configuration.
